subject.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)

question: Should OpenClaw merge this disabled-by-default host-side abandonment timeout as the permanent mitigation, or require a default-on cooperative context-engine cancellation contract first?
rationale: Code review can validate the fence and persistence mechanics, but it cannot choose the product compatibility policy for long-running plugins, a new config surface, or execution that continues after the lane is released.

options.title: Sponsor the opt-in mitigation
options.body: Merge the current disabled-by-default design and explicitly define the timeout as host-side abandonment that fences OpenClaw-owned effects without claiming to stop plugin execution.

options.title: Require cooperative cancellation
options.body: Hold the PR until the context-engine contract exposes a host-owned abort or release mechanism with a chosen default and fresh-install plus upgrade proof.

options.title: Pause the new surfaces
options.body: Close or narrow the PR if maintainers do not want another compaction config key and generic queue callback, while retaining the diagnostic-backoff work separately.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the opt-in mitigation
recommendation.body: Merge the current disabled-by-default design and explicitly define the timeout as host-side abandonment that fences OpenClaw-owned effects without claiming to stop plugin execution.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision primarily governs the context-engine and compaction contract, the area assigned to this owner in repository guidance.
